a32_presign.redirect_shape: 307 Temporary Redirect from the api, one per object. Playlists (master.m3u8, media_N.m3u8) and storyboard.vtt are never redirected - delivery.Redirectable is false for them - so presigned URLs are NEVER written into a playlist; the player fetches every child URI from the api and takes a 307 per segment.
a32_presign.preflight: none observed in either browser: the segment request is same-origin to the api and only becomes cross-origin after the 307, and a single 'bytes=' Range is a CORS-safelisted request header, so no OPTIONS is sent and the CORS check lands on the response

webkit_presign_on.src: blob: (MSE - WebKit does not take a native-HLS path here)

a32_presign.range: GET /original presigned with Range: bytes=0-99 -> 206, content-range bytes 0-99/151951, cross-origin, Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoed

expiry.past_ttl: 403 AccessDenied - 'Request has expired' (measured on a lab build with an 8-second TTL)
expiry.recovery: the client re-requests the api route, which mints a fresh signature - measured 200 immediately after the 403
expiry.cached_redirect_can_never_outlive_the_si: the 307's own Cache-Control is private, max-age=300 and the signature lasts 3600s; within the 300s window the browser re-dereferences nothing at all (the presigned response body is cached under the same directive), measured by fetching the same segment route twice 12s apart and seeing one 307 and one bucket GET

a32_presign.credentialed_reads: Authorization header -> 200 on the proxy with private, no-store and no Location; the A08 rule holds under presign

cache_control.api_playlists: private, max-age=0, must-revalidate unversioned; private, max-age=31536000, immutable with ?v=

edge_response.content_disposition: absent, so a download loses its filename

cache_control.reading: nothing becomes public, by design (internal/delivery: promotion is gated on Purge being exercised). But the api's header never governs the edge: the edge pulls from the BUCKET at the object's own key, and Vidra writes no cache metadata on stored objects at all - so edge caching is governed entirely by the CDN's default TTL with no Vidra input, and with three purge families open that TTL is the only bound on stale media.

origin_exposure.requirement: a key-addressed CDN origin must be readable by the edge; done the obvious way (an anonymous download policy on the bucket) every object becomes world-readable at the origin
origin_exposure.no_prefix_separates_them: public and private media share web-videos/, thumbnails/ and streaming-playlists/
origin_exposure.purge_is_undone: after the privacy flip's successful 18-key purge, the next edge fetch of the now-private poster was a MISS that re-pulled 1604 bytes from the origin and cached them again
origin_exposure.docs: neither .env.example nor docs/operations.md warns about this; both say only that eligible media is HANDED to the edge
